//: Cases for `python tools/toolcheck.py`. Data, not code, exactly like
//1: deploy.json -- adding a case must not require touching the runner.
//5: why      the bug this case exists to stop coming back. Required.
//6: needs    'any' | 'menu' (client at the main menu) | 'raid' (in a raid)
//7: write    true if the batch needs liveInspectorWrite + 'allow write'
//8: batches  list of batches. SEPARATE batches on purpose: per-batch
//9: anchors ($comp, $f1) do NOT survive across batches, and one
//10: of the historical bugs was exactly that they seemed to.
//11: assert   regexes that MUST appear in the normalised answer
//12: refuse   regexes that MUST appear AND are declared to be a REFUSAL.
//13: Reported separately, because 'the tool correctly declined'
//14: is the behaviour half these bugs broke, and a case with no
//15: refuse entry cannot lock it in.
//16: deny     regexes that must NOT appear -- the WRONG answer's shape.
//17: A refuse case without a deny is weak: it proves the
//18: refusal was printed, not that no answer was also printed.
//20: Answers are NORMALISED before matching: every pointer becomes <PTR>,
//21: every count-of-nodes/ms becomes <N>. Assert on names, shapes, counts
//22: and the FORM of an answer. Never on an address -- they change per run
//23: and an address assertion fails for a reason that is not a regression.

cases.name: channel-alive
cases.why: If the channel is dead every other case 'passes' by matching nothing. This must run first and its failure aborts the suite.

cases.name: roots-shape
cases.why: `roots` is how everything is reached. Its answer shape (transform + GameObject + name, two distinct anchors) is the contract every other case depends on.

cases.name: roots-lists-menu-ui
cases.why: The live UI is in DontDestroyOnLoad, which SceneManager excludes. Before `roots`, `find` searched only $preloader's subtree and reported names 'NOT PRESENT' that were merely unreachable.

cases.name: find-stopped-early-is-not-absence
cases.why: A bounded search that ran out of budget must SAY SO. Reporting a name as absent when the search merely stopped is a confidently-wrong answer.

cases.name: find-exhaustive-says-so
cases.why: The other half of the same contract: a search that DID cover the tree must be distinguishable from one that did not, or 'not found' means nothing.

cases.name: component-null-is-an-answer
cases.why: A failed component lookup must be reported as an ANSWER, not swallowed. When it was swallowed, $comp kept the PREVIOUS batch's pointer.

cases.name: comp-anchor-not-stale
cases.why: THE bug: a failed `component` left $comp holding the previous lookup's pointer, so the next `click`/`dump` acted on the wrong object and printed a complete, entirely fictional field map.

cases.name: gameobject-into-transform-walker-refused
cases.why: Feeding a GameObject to a Transform walker used to read a plausible childCount and INVENT a hierarchy of wrong children without faulting. Silence would be better; a refusal is correct.

cases.name: label-on-transform-is-not-empty-text
cases.why: `label` on a Transform reported `text = ""`, which reads as 'the label is empty' and is not an answer. It must say there is no text component.

cases.name: click-refuses-a-non-button
cases.why: `click`/`invoke` imposed UnityEngine.UI.Button's layout on ANY pointer, calling UnityEvent::Invoke on a GameObject and escaping the guard.

cases.name: write-gate-holds-without-allow-write
cases.why: liveInspectorWrite alone must not be enough; the batch must also say `allow write`. A write that goes through without it means the gate is decorative.

cases.name: open-refusal-names-a-reason
cases.why: `open` rejected a CORRECT target because the prologue snapshot had recorded our own trampoline. A refusal is acceptable; a refusal with no stated reason is not, because it is indistinguishable from that bug.

cases.name: state-explains-every-null-anchor
cases.why: `state` exists to say WHY an anchor is null. An anchor listed as null with no reason sends you hunting for an object the host simply has not learned yet.

cases.name: state-does-not-claim-not-in-raid-from-a-slot
cases.why: fact #51: `state` reported `in-raid anchor slot=-1` while a human WAS in a raid. A slot number is the anchor's binding, not the raid state, and must never be printed as if it were the raid state.

cases.name: state-settings-null-does-not-invent-a-cause
cases.why: `state` asserted the SettingsScreen anchor was null because the screen 'has not been opened this session' while the host log showed ShowScreen already firing and $settings still null -- a cause it never checked. The message must name what it actually knows (two independent hooks, either can be un-armed) rather than a single invented cause.

cases.name: find-single-numeric-arg-is-budget-not-root
cases.why: `find NAME 200000` silently read 200000 decimal (0x30d40) as a ROOT pointer, walked that one bogus node, and reported the name genuinely NOT PRESENT. A bare integer that does not read back as a live pointer must be treated as BUDGET and the tool must say which interpretation it picked.

cases.name: find-invalid-root-refused-not-reported-absent
cases.why: An explicit root that does not read back as a live Transform must be refused up front, the way `tree` already refuses -- never walked as if valid and then reported 'searched EXHAUSTIVELY, genuinely NOT PRESENT' off one bogus node.

cases.name: findtext-single-numeric-arg-is-budget-not-root
cases.why: `findtext` had its own copy of the ROOT-vs-BUDGET parser from BEFORE this ambiguity was fixed in `find`: `findtext SETTINGS 300000` silently read 300000 decimal (0x493e0) as a ROOT, walked one bogus node, and claimed the text genuinely NOT PRESENT. Now shares `find`'s readability-based disambiguator (`iFindResolveRoot`).

cases.name: findtext-invalid-root-refused-not-reported-absent
cases.why: `findtext` accepted an unreadable explicit root and then asserted a confident, exhaustive absence from it. It must refuse up front, the same as `find` and `tree` already do.

cases.name: findtext-echoes-once-not-per-frame
cases.why: A frame-spanning `findtext` re-entered iExec every frame and the echo-suppression check only ever covered `find`'s resume flag, so a 57-frame findtext search printed 57 identical `> findtext ...` header lines around a 4-line answer.

cases.name: findtext-hit-reports-active-state-and-scope
cases.why: findtext hits gave no way to tell an active, pressable control from an inactive one -- pressing an inactive node returns success and does nothing (fact #72). A hit must state activeInHierarchy, and the summary must state which scope (active-only vs all) was actually searched.

cases.name: rect-decodes-vector2-and-rect-struct-returns
cases.why: `rect` used to call the Vector2/Rect getters and admit it could not decode a struct-BY-VALUE return, pointing at a `fields` workaround that measurement showed is impossible on RectTransform (only one il2cpp field, reapplyDrivenProperties). This asserts the numbers now print instead of the old disclaimer.
deny: call shapes do not decode yet

cases.name: tab-refuses-a-wrong-receiver-type
cases.why: MEASURED: `tab` fed an EFT.UI.AnimatedToggle and then a UnityEngine.CanvasRenderer called SettingsTab::set_IsSelected on both, wrote +0x90 on objects with no such field, printed a plausible 'first-select latch' line, and desynced the Settings screen (escapes=1). A typed call on an untyped pointer must refuse by KLASS.

cases.name: tab-drives-the-toggle-not-the-highlight
cases.why: Even on a REAL SettingsTab the old `tab` moved the highlight and not the panel: the screen switches on the toggle's onValueChanged, not on set_IsSelected. The verb must name Toggle::set_isOn and must read _currentTab back as the finished state.
assert: SELECT A TAB THE WAY A CLICK DOES

cases.name: open-unknown-group-is-refused-not-zero
cases.why: MEASURED: `open Graphics` opened Game. An unrecognised name was evaluated as an expression, the failed parse's return was DISCARDED, and group stayed 0 -- a check that cannot fail. An unknown name must refuse and list the valid ones.

cases.name: open-accepts-group-names-case-insensitively
cases.why: The fix for the above must actually map the names, not just refuse everything. `graphics` is ESettingsGroup.Screen = 0 (measured from metadata), which is the mapping the reporter expected and did not get.

cases.name: open-refuses-a-screen-that-is-not-active
cases.why: MEASURED: `open N` immediately after pressing BACK ran ShowScreen on a screen mid-close and ESCAPED the SEH guard (escapes=1). $settings survives a close -- the same pointer comes back on reopen -- so a non-null pointer proves nothing about callability. activeInHierarchy is the state that differs.

cases.name: find-cap-message-names-the-real-limiter
cases.why: MEASURED: a search that visited 30,720 of an 80,000 node budget printed 'STOPPED EARLY on the NODE BUDGET', sending the reader to raise a budget with 49,280 nodes still unspent. The frame cap and the node budget are different limiters and the message must say which one fired.
assert: (searched EXHAUSTIVELY|STOPPED EARLY on the (FRAME CAP|NODE BUDGET))
deny: STOPPED EARLY on the NODE BUDGET \(80000\)[\s\S]*budget still has room

cases.name: parent-level-0-is-the-node-you-passed
cases.why: Reported inconsistent: `parent <SettingsList> 1` printed the node itself as [0] in one call and the PARENT as [0] in another. The numbering is now a stated contract, printed on every call, and a GameObject argument (the reachable cause) is refused.

cases.name: pressname-fail-names-the-failing-check
cases.why: MEASURED: pressname found exactly one VISIBLE candidate and printed 'could not be pressed (see the line above)' with no reason findable in the out-file -- while the same object pressed fine by hand via component+press. A verdict that points at absent evidence is worse than no verdict.
assert: a FAIL prints the failing check ON THE VERDICT LINE

cases.name: pressname-resumes-until-exhaustive
cases.why: MEASURED: `pressname BackButton` with no root visited 20,000 nodes in ONE slice, left a ~13-15k frontier, and reported '0 name match(es) ... INCONCLUSIVE' for a button that was on screen. One frame is smaller than the scene.

cases.name: roots-reaches-dontdestroyonload-in-a-raid
cases.why: MEASURED in a live Woods raid: `roots` returned only the location scene (woods_terrain, AICoversData, Location Scene, ...) and rootless `find MenuScreen 80000` + two `find more` answered 'searched EXHAUSTIVELY ... genuinely NOT PRESENT' for a live screen. PreloaderUI does not tick in a raid, so the DDOL anchor is dead; the handle is now remembered and revalidated by name.

cases.name: roots-at-the-menu-still-lists-the-ddol-set
cases.why: The in-raid fix must not change the menu answer. A regression here would mean the remembered handle displaced the live anchor rather than backing it up.

cases.name: raid-verb-refuses-inside-a-raid
cases.why: The raid-entry state machine walks the MENU hierarchy; running it during a raid load stalls the Unity thread (fact #261). A live GameWorld is a POSITIVE test for being in a raid -- the converse is deliberately not asserted.

cases.name: raid-verb-arms-at-the-menu
cases.why: The user's verdict on outside-driven UI automation was that it is far too slow; the host-native path is ~970ms menu-to-READY. The verb must ARM it and must say that armed is not entered.

cases.name: raidexit-refuses-when-not-in-a-raid
cases.why: raidexit presses DISCONNECT. Outside a raid there is nothing to disconnect from, and it must prove being in one positively (a live GameWorld) rather than inferring it from scene roots -- which is exactly the inference that was measured wrong in a raid.

cases.name: click-refuses-by-klass-not-only-by-field-shape
cases.why: click's GameObject-in-m_OnClick and klass-pointer checks are inferences from values at Button's offsets; a UnityEngine.CanvasRenderer has neither at +0x100 and would have passed both. The receiver's klass chain is the direct question.
